text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday Albanian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The United States of America has urged Albania to hold fresh general elections and added it was deeply concerned over growing disorder in Albania following a financial scandal.
- U.S. ambassador in Tirana Marisa Lino said she would not go to parliament when it elects a new president. She added the U.S. stand did not differ from the European Union position.
- The European Union has offered Albania financial aid to overcome a financial and institutional crisis if Tirana cooperates with the International Monetary Fund.
- Thousands of students in Tirana have boycotted lessons to support fasting students in Vlore who want the government to resign over the collapse of pyramid investment scams.

- The tiny Republican Party wants parliament to discuss a hunger strike by students calling for the resignation of the government before it sets a date for the election of a new president. Whereas the National Front Party wants the term of President Sali Berisha extended for one more year.

- The ruling Democratic Party confirmed it had received a legal donation of $50,000 from the failed Gjallica scheme early in 1996 but said it had then no information it was a pyramid scheme. It added it would return the money.
- The Albanian lek continued to weaken on Tuesday, fixed at 141 to the U.S. dollar.
- Marisa Lino, the U.S. envoy to Tirana said her country's insistence Albania should hold fresh general elections was based on the reported violations of the May 26 polls.
- Ten fasting students in Vlore have been forced to go to hospital after their health deteriorated.

- President Sali Berisha promised to lift taxes for farmers in the southern town of Berat, hit by a financial crisis after pyramid investment scams collapsed, and create conditions for the development of tourism there.
